context: Flow map of US domestic migration between 12 major cities, with directed curved arrows sized by volume, nodes colored/sized by net migration (blue=growing, red=shrinking), and animated dash overlays showing flow direction.
first_impression: The map projection is catastrophically broken — the US outline renders as a giant horseshoe occupying most of the canvas while all 12 cities are crushed into a tiny ~150px cluster in the lower-center, making the geographic basis of the visualization completely illegible.
what_works: The two-color encoding (blue/red) for net migration direction is clean and unambiguous; the hover-to-isolate interaction design is conceptually sound, dimming unrelated flows and coloring outbound red vs inbound blue.
what_doesnt: The geoAlbers projection misconfiguration causes the continental US silhouette to fill the viewport as a distorted crescent, compressing all city nodes into an unreadable pile where labels overlap and individual arrow paths cannot be traced; the animated dash overlay on 28 simultaneously moving paths adds visual noise that cannot be perceptually evaluated from a static screenshot but will compound the spatial confusion.
